extracted.intended_audience: students, teachers, and readers/scholars of American literature and literary history
extracted.subtask_description: Biographical and bibliographic entries for American writers with reading suggestions, studies/reviews, and classified indexes to guide literary study and research. Useful for constructing reading lists, comparative study, and locating secondary literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare Mrs. Wharton with Henry James
rubrics_metrics.description: Mrs. Wharton's friendship with Henry James and the derivation of her methods from his suggest an interesting comparison of the work of these two writers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "For this comparison, books treating of similar material should be chosen; for example, Mrs. Wharton's The Custom of the Country or Madame de Treymes with Mr. James's Portrait of a Lady or The Ambassadors. The result will show that Mrs. Wharton, having an essentially different type of mind, has worked out an interesting set of variations of Mr. James's method." (Use paired texts treating similar material to reveal method/variation.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Study and judge different types of Wharton's novels separately
rubrics_metrics.description: Mrs. Wharton's novels of American social life should be studied and judged separately from her Italian historical novel (The Valley of Decision) and from her New England stories, Ethan Frome and Summer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat different subgenres/subjects within an author's oeuvre as distinct critical domains rather than conflating them into a single judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine specific recurring phases/themes (supernatural, satire)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two special phases of Mrs. Wharton's work which call for study are her management of supernatural effects in some of her short stories and her use of satire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus analytical attention on how particular techniques (e.g., supernatural management, satiric mode) operate within the author's work and what they reveal about method and effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use comparative short-story analysis with contemporary disciples
rubrics_metrics.description: Her short stories offer a basis of comparison with those of Mrs. Gerould (q.v.), another disciple of Mr. James.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare stories by authors in the same critical lineage to trace influences, divergences, and differing applications of methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess originality and lasting significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Has Mrs. Wharton enough originality and enough distinction to hold a permanent high place as a novelist of American manners?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make a judgment about an author's originality and potential for permanent standing by weighing distinctive qualities, innovation, and overall achievement in their principal subject-matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Carl Van Doren's criticisms as a basis for critical judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the following criticisms by Mr. Carl Van Doren as the basis of a critical judgment of your own; decide whether he is in all respects right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted guidance (Carl Van Doren): "From the first Mrs. Wharton's power has lain in the ability to reproduce in fiction the circumstances of a compact community in a way that illustrates the various oppressions which such communities put upon individual vagaries, whether viewed as sin, or ignorance, or folly, or merely as social impossibility. She has always been singularly unpartisan... It is only in these moments of satire that Mrs. Wharton reveals much about her disposition... If she had a little less of this pride of dignity she might perhaps avoid her tendency to assign to decorum a larger power than it actually exercises... The illusion of reality in her work, however, almost never fails her, so alertly is her mind on the lookout to avoid vulgar or shoddy romantic elements." (Use this set of claims as focal points to confirm, refute, or nuance in one’s own critique.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult listed studies, periodical reviews, and Book Review Digest for reception history
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries include a 'STUDIES AND REVIEWS' section and repeated instruction to 'See also Book Review Digest' for contemporary criticism and reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the cited journals and the Book Review Digest as primary means to locate contemporary critical reception and secondary literature (examples in the text: Dial, Poetry, New Republic, Nation, Lit. Digest, Bookman, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the book's classified-index scheme for locating authors by role/subject/place
rubrics_metrics.description: This volume provides classified indexes (I–XII) grouping authors by role (Poets; Dramatists; Novelists; Short-story writers; Essayists; Critics; etc.), by subjects, and by place of birth; authors appear in the body alphabetically and page references are omitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using the compendium: rely on alphabetical body entries for full bios and on the classified indexes for lookup by genre/role, subject area, or geographic origin; note the procedural remark: 'Since the authors appear in the body of the book in alphabetical order, page references have been omitted in these indexes.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliographic-entry conventions and brief work-type annotations
rubrics_metrics.description: Bibliographies for each author list works with year and sometimes parenthetical notes indicating form or series (e.g., (Novel), (Play), (Travel), _Chronicles of America Series_).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the bibliography lines to identify primary works, their publication dates, and the form/genre; starred items and parenthetical notes flag notable works or formats (the page shows starred titles but does not define the star here).
